text:
ajay: Quick thought — should we keep header-free requests routed to v1 as a temporary 'grace mode' with a small quota that doesn't eat into their v1 committed capacity? We saw a spike where mobile SDKs didn't set X-Redwood-API-Version and started failing.

tori: probably yes for a short window, but console needs to surface who is on grace mode. otherwise support will drown.

sam: agree on the surface. also we need telemetry that tags fallback_reason=missing_version so we can filter signals cleanly.

kevin: if we create exemptions we must not silently inflate customers' committed usage. Suggest we route to v1 but count against a dedicated compat_quota line item that shows in billing/usage. That keeps accounting clean.

ajay: compat_quota sounds perfect. Console UX: show a small 'compat mode' pill in per-customer usage and in the per-route breakdown, with a link to migration docs.

tori: and alert when compat_quota > 10% of monthly token usage for a customer so PM/CS can reach out.

sam: implementation note: runtime will set header X-Compat-Route=true when we fall through. Example request snippet: 
```
GET /v1/generate
Headers: {"X-Redwood-API-Version": "", "X-Compat-Route": "true"}
```

kevin: we'll also need to tag billing pipeline records with compat_quota so cost attribution matches. Opening a billing ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy started for compat-fallthrough-probe -> canary on us-east-1 (build: compat-probe-2026-03-20)

ajay: can we add a telemetry event id: compat_fallthrough.probe with fields: customer_id, route, reason, token_count, schema_check_passed? Sam pls add to telemetry schema.

sam: on it. quick question: how long should the probe run? propose 7 days with auto-escalate to outreach at 7 days.

tori: 7 days seems reasonable for most customers. we can extend to 14 for enterprise accounts on request.

kevin: corner case: function-calling differences between v1/v2 — runtime should perform a lightweight schema compatibility check; if mismatch, return 422 + telemetry instead of routing silently.

ajay: agreed. runtime will run schema_check and only route if compatible. If not, respond 422 with body {"error":"incompatible-api-schema","hint":"set X-Redwood-API-Version or upgrade SDK"} and emit compat_fallthrough.schema_mismatch.

tori: can we add an opt-out toggle in console per-account? Legal asked for explicit opt-out for regulated customers.

ajay: add opt-out in account settings (default: allow). We'll document in rollout playbook and migration checklist.

sam: I'll add dashboard tiles: compat_fallthrough rate over time, top customers by compat_quota, and schema_mismatch counts.

kevin: opened billing ticket (#BILL-482) to add compat_quota tag to cost records.

ajay: thanks — I'll draft the announcement copy and the runbook. Quick summary to post in #announcements once we finalize UI copy: 'Temporarily routing requests without API-version to v1 for 7 days; customers will see a compat_quota line item and console badge; opt-out available.' :thumbsup:
